With our three market‑leading businesses, world‑class operations, and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense. This position is part of RTX Enterprise Services within Digital Technology, on the Disaster Readiness and Recovery team. As an Enterprise Disaster Recovery Planning & Strategy Consultant, you will occupy a highly technical and strategically consultative role at the intersection of application architecture, infrastructure, and business continuity. You will lead the design and refinement of the Application Recovery Plan (ARP) framework, advise application and platform teams on recovery strategies, and influence how recovery dependencies and scenarios are engineered across RTX. This role combines deep technical engagement (e.g., understanding application architectures, dependencies, and recovery patterns) with senior‑level advisory responsibilities to shape disaster recovery strategy, planning standards, and stakeholder decision‑making. The role will also include leadership and coaching of a small team of DR planning professionals, along with additional responsibility for prioritization and execution oversight. What You Will Do Design, refine, and drive the implementation of the enterprise ARP framework, including standards, templates, guidance, and quality criteria for application recovery planning. Provide technical and strategic consulting to application, infrastructure, and platform teams on viable recovery strategies, RTO/RPO alignment, dependency modeling, and recovery sequencing. Lead or facilitate deep‑dive working sessions with architects, engineers, and service owners to identify recovery requirements, technical constraints, and dependency risks. Partner with application owners, Infrastructure & Workplace Services, cybersecurity, and business stakeholders to develop, review, and maintain high‑quality ARPs that are technically sound and aligned to enterprise objectives. Identify, assess, and document technical recovery dependencies (e.g., databases, middleware, identity, network, storage, shared services) and their impact on recovery ordering and feasibility. Evaluate ARPs and related technical documentation to identify gaps, inconsistencies, architectural risks, and opportunities to improve resilience. Support and help lead disaster recovery readiness assessments, planning exercises, and scenario‑based walk‑throughs, providing expert input on technical and architectural implications. Collaborate with Disaster Readiness and Recovery leadership to inform DR strategy, roadmap, and standards, based on observed patterns, dependency risks, and emerging technology constraints. Contribute to the definition of reference architectures, patterns, and best practices for highly recoverable applications and services. Develop and maintain consultative relationships with senior stakeholders (e.g., product owners, platform leads, enterprise architects) to influence design and investment decisions in support of resilience. Support onboarding, training, and knowledge transfer activities related to ARP standards, technical expectations, and DR planning practices. Communicate planning progress, risk insights, recovery dependencies, and recommended actions to program leadership and other decision‑makers in clear, business‑relevant terms. Provide day‑to‑day leadership and coaching to a team of DR planning and readiness professionals. Translate DR strategy into team‑level objectives, work plans, and priorities, ensuring alignment with broader Disaster Readiness and Recovery goals. Oversee work allocation, quality reviews, and development of team members, fostering a culture of technical excellence and consultative engagement. Qualifications You Must Have Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 8 years of prior relevant experience, or an Advanced Degree in a related field and a minimum of 5 years of experience. Experience supporting enterprise technology, application, or infrastructure initiatives with a strong emphasis on resiliency, availability, or continuity. Demonstrated experience coordinating cross‑functional activities involving application owners, architects, engineers, and business stakeholders Qualifications We Prefer Significant experience with enterprise disaster recovery, business continuity, IT resilience, or application recovery planning. Proven ability to gather, interpret, and structure business and technical requirements into actionable plans or designs. Strong understanding of modern application and infrastructure architectures (e.g., multi‑tier applications, databases, middleware, cloud/on‑prem hybrid, networking and identity services) and how they influence recovery approaches. Familiarity with Application Recovery Plans (ARPs), recovery strategies, dependency modeling, and impact analysis. Experience performing or leading technical DR readiness assessments, tabletop exercises, or scenario‑based recovery planning. Experience contributing to governance frameworks, technical standards, and architecture patterns related to resilience and recoverability. Excellent consultative, communication, and stakeholder‑influencing skills, including the ability to translate complex technical issues into clear, risk‑based recommendations. Strong analytical and systems thinking skills, with the ability to identify cross‑application dependencies, chokepoints, and systemic risks. Prior people leadership experience (formal or strong matrix) in disaster recovery, architecture, or related technical domains. Demonstrated ability to set team direction, manage workload, and deliver results in a large, matrixed enterprise environment. Some of the benefits we offer include parental (including paternal) leave, flexible work schedules, achievement awards, educational assistance, and child/adult backup care.
